correctness.rationale: The weighted-Laplacian inverse power trace is strictly convex for p=1,2 on connected support, and edge Laplacian directions are injective; this proves unrestricted uniqueness. Rim rotations yield precisely two edge classes. Their complete nonzero Fourier spectrum gives one-variable strictly convex objectives with interior minima. The seven finite separator sign pairs were recomputed by exact Fraction Gaussian elimination from the standalone verify.py (127 checks total). For all m>=11, Poisson-kernel cycle resolvent identities imply Phi1_prime(1/3)<0 and Phi2_prime(1/3)>0 by explicit universal inequalities; K4 gives equality at m=3. Limiting integrals yield u1->1/3, u2->(sqrt(7)-2)/3 and ratio 1.045942437429. Finite checks are supplemental, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The first and squared inverse Laplacian traces are natural, inequivalent performance criteria for first- and second-order noisy consensus under one common edge budget. Exact all-size global optimization reveals a strict direction reversal at precisely the 6-to-7-rim boundary, which cannot be inferred from a single-objective optimum. The persistent 4.594 percent second-order penalty of reusing the first-order asymptotic design has a direct and precisely scoped decision interpretation, without claiming broader network generality.
